title: The Legends Timeline
lede: Twenty-five years of the Marvel Legends line — Toy Biz's clamshell launch in 2002 to the retro-blister era of 2026. Every wave below links into the archive; every historical claim carries its source.

years.headline: The line launches
years.summary: Marvel Legends debuts as a Toy Biz spin-off of the Spider-Man Classics line, aimed at adult collectors with best-in-class sculpt and articulation. Series 1 through 3 plus Walmart exclusives ship in oversized clamshells, each with a 32-page reprint comic book.
years.packaging: Oversized clamshell with 32-page reprint comic pack-in.

milestones.text: The line begins in 2002 as a spin-off of Spider-Man Classics, copying its clamshell packaging and included comic book.
The first wave ships: Iron Man, Captain America, and Hulk, with Toad as the villain.

spotlight.name: Captain America
spotlight.why: Series 1 launch figure — the wave that started the line.

years.headline: Box sets arrive
years.summary: Series 4 and 5 keep the numbered line rolling while Toy Biz experiments with big-ticket multipacks: the X-Men Legends and Urban Legends box sets.

years.headline: The numbered line grows
years.summary: Series 6, 7, and 8 deepen the roster, and the box-set program continues with Spider-Man vs. the Sinister 6 and a Fantastic Four set.

years.headline: Build-A-Figure is born
years.summary: Series 9 (the Galactus series) packs one piece of a 16-inch Galactus with every figure — the Build-A-Figure is born. The Sentinel and Apocalypse series follow the same playbook, and the Legendary Riders and Fearsome Foes box sets round out the year. Behind the scenes, Marvel terminates the Toy Biz Worldwide license a year early, paying a $13–16M penalty.

milestones.text: Series 9 introduces the Build-A-Figure: each figure carries a piece of a larger figure, so buying the full assortment assembles a character unavailable on its own — here, a 16-inch Galactus.
Marvel terminates the Toy Biz Worldwide license a year early, paying a $13–16M penalty.

waves.series: Box Set - Spider-Man vs. The Fearsome Foes

spotlight.name: Bullseye
spotlight.why: A Series 9 carrier — the wave that debuted Build-A-Figure.

years.headline: Toy Biz's last stand
years.summary: The final Toy Biz year is a blaze of glory: Series 13 (Onslaught), 14 (Mojo), and 15 (M.O.D.O.K.), a Walmart-exclusive Giant-Man, and House of M, Monsters, and Young Avengers box sets. The Face-Off 2-pack program pairs arch-enemies, and the 12-inch Legends Icons line launches with Captain America, Iron Man, Wolverine, Hulk, Venom, Beast, and Spider-Man. Marvel grants Hasbro a 5-year master toy license — $205M in guaranteed royalties with a $100M non-refundable advance — with retail sales to begin January 1, 2007.

sources.label: Legendsverse — Face-Off Captain America & Red Skull (2006)
FigureRealm — Face-Off Cap vs Red Skull

milestones.text: Face-Off 2-packs debut: Series 1 pairs Hulk vs. Leader, Captain America vs. Red Skull, and Daredevil vs. Kingpin; Series 2 adds Punisher vs. Jigsaw, Wolverine vs. Sabretooth, and the Iron Man/War Machine vs. Mandarin sets.
Marvel Legends Icons launches: 12-inch figures with over 30 points of articulation and an 'Evolution of an Icon' comic-sized book per character.
Marvel grants Hasbro a 5-year master toy license: $205M guaranteed royalties, $100M non-refundable advance. Retail sales begin January 1, 2007.

spotlight.name: Captain America
spotlight.why: Face-Off Series 1 — arch-enemy pairings were 2006's signature program.

years.headline: Hasbro takes over
years.summary: The Hasbro era begins January 1, 2007. New packaging drops the comic book pack-in and new molds eliminate Toy Biz's signature finger joints — but the Build-A-Figure theme continues with the Annihilus, Blob, Ronan, Brood Queen, and Sandman (Spider-Man 3) waves, plus the first SDCC and store exclusives.
years.packaging: Blister card; comic pack-in dropped; finger joints eliminated on new molds.

milestones.text: Hasbro becomes the license holder on January 1, 2007. The new packaging drops the comic book, new molds eliminate finger joints — a mainstay of the Toy Biz era — and the company continues the Build-A-Figure theme.

years.headline: Big dragons, red Hulks
years.summary: The Fin Fang Foom wave anchors the year, with a Target-exclusive Red Hulk wave, a Walmart-exclusive Ares wave, 2-packs, and an SDCC Fin Fang Foom box set.

waves.series: SDCC Box Set - Fin Fang Foom

years.headline: The quiet years begin
years.summary: Output slows to a trickle — a Walmart-exclusive Nemesis wave and 2-packs Series 2 are the whole year. Hasbro launches the 3.75-inch Marvel Universe line, and production on Legends slows to the point that cancellation is rumored.

milestones.text: During the late 2000s, production on the Marvel Legends line slows to the point where cancellation is rumored.
Hasbro launches Marvel Universe, an iconic 3.75-inch articulated line (nearly 84 figures between 2009 and 2013).

years.headline: The comeback announced
years.summary: The archive holds only Toys 'R' Us 2-packs this year — but at SDCC 2010, Hasbro announces the line's full return for 2012, citing fan demand and the upcoming Marvel movies.

milestones.text: At SDCC 2010, Hasbro reveals that due to fan requests and upcoming Marvel movies, the line will make a comeback in 2012.

years.headline: One Thor
years.summary: The archive's entire 2011 is a single SDCC Thor exclusive. The comeback is a year out.

years.headline: The Return of Marvel Legends
years.summary: All-new sculpts return to store shelves in January 2012. The Terrax and Arnim Zola waves carry 'The Return of Marvel Legends' stickers, and SDCC gets an Uncanny X-Force box set.

milestones.text: In January 2012, Marvel Legends returns to store shelves; the Terrax and Arnim Zola waves carry 'The Return of Marvel Legends' stickers.

waves.series: Arnim Zola Wave (Return of Marvel Legends)

spotlight.name: Hope Summers
spotlight.why: A standout new-character debut in the Return wave.

years.headline: Mini BAFs
years.summary: A named Epic Heroes wave (not the later 4-inch kid line), plus Iron Monger, Hit-Monkey, and Rocket Raccoon waves — the Hit-Monkey, Rocket Raccoon, and Jubilee waves use the 'Mini' Build-A-Figure concept. Puck arrives as a Previews exclusive.

milestones.text: The Hit-Monkey, Rocket Raccoon, and Jubilee waves use the 'Mini' Build-A-Figure concept.

years.headline: Infinite Series relaunch
years.summary: The line is retooled as Marvel Legends: Infinite Series at a $19.99 MSRP — box packaging, bigger BAFs, more accessories. The Mandroid, Ultimate Green Goblin, and Groot waves lead; a Toys 'R' Us-exclusive Jubilee wave uses the mini-BAF concept.
years.packaging: Window box replaces the blister card; bigger BAFs, more accessories.

milestones.text: Retooled as Marvel Legends: Infinite Series at $19.99 MSRP — box packaging, bigger BAFs, more accessories.

spotlight.name: Rocket
spotlight.why: The Guardians-era Groot wave — a flagship of the relaunch year.

years.headline: The BAF blockbusters
years.summary: Big-build year: Thanos (Infinity), Ultron Prime and the Hulkbuster (Age of Ultron), Rhino, Hobgoblin, and the Allfather waves.

years.headline: Photo-real faces
years.summary: Photo-real face-printing arrives for likenesses, alongside butterfly joints. The Absorbing Man, Red Onslaught, Giant-Man (Civil War), Space Knight Venom, Abomination, Juggernaut, and Dormammu waves fill the shelves.

milestones.text: Photo-real face-printing for likenesses; butterfly joints debut. Pinless joints arrive around 2020 and become standard.

spotlight.name: Rogue
spotlight.why: The Juggernaut wave — Rogue's modern Legends look.

years.headline: MCU tie-in peak
years.summary: Movie waves dominate: Vulture (Homecoming), Mantis (Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2), and Gladiator Hulk (Thor: Ragnarok) alongside comics waves — Sandman, Titus, Warlock (New Mutants), and Man-Thing.

years.headline: Infinity War year
years.summary: Ten waves — the biggest year in the archive by figure count. Okoye, Thanos, and Cull Obsidian ride Avengers: Infinity War; Lizard, Sasquatch, Apocalypse, SP//dr, Monster Venom, and Sauron cover the comics side.

years.headline: Retro X-Men
years.summary: Hasbro unveils Uncanny X-Men figures on throwback '90s-style cards as part of the Marvel 80th anniversary — Wolverine, Silver Samurai, Cyclops, Dazzler, Storm, and Iceman — with pre-orders opening in June and shipping slated for August. The M'Baku, Kree Sentry, Kingpin, Armored Thanos (Endgame), Caliban, Smart Hulk, Molten Man (Far From Home), Wendigo, and Fat Thor waves fill the year.

milestones.text: Hasbro unveils Uncanny X-Men figures with '90s-style throwback cards as part of the Marvel 80th anniversary lineup — Wolverine, Silver Samurai, Cyclops, Dazzler, Storm, and Iceman.

years.headline: HasLab era begins
years.summary: The first Marvel Legends HasLab: a 26.3-inch Sentinel at $349.99, funded in about 24 hours. Mainline waves include Super-Skrull, Demogoblin, Crimson Dynamo, the Gamerverse Abomination, Venompool, and Joe Fixit waves, plus Sugar Man and Strong Guy. Hasbro also launches the 3.75-inch Marvel Legends RETRO line via Pulse two-packs, and at Toy Fair 2020 the X-Men movie likenesses finally join the 6-inch line.

milestones.text: First ML HasLab: 26.3-inch Sentinel at $349.99, funded in ~24 hours.

sources.label: Marvel Toys Wiki — Marvel Legends RETRO

milestones.text: Hasbro launches Marvel Legends RETRO, a 3.75-inch Kenner-style sister line — first as Pulse-exclusive two-packs (Cyclops, Captain America, Electro), then as a full line in 2021 starting as a timed Target exclusive.
At Toy Fair 2020, Hasbro reveals X-Men movie likenesses for the line — Wolverine, Mystique, Professor X, Magneto (with dual-era head sculpts), plus the Deadpool 2 cast.

years.headline: Galactus towers
years.summary: The 32-inch Galactus HasLab at $399.99 draws 14,000 backers — the biggest Marvel Legends ever. The Stilt-Man, Tri-Sentinel, Mr. Hyde, Flight Gear, Xemnu, Ursa Major, Colossus (Age of Apocalypse), Watcher (What If...?), Gilgamesh (Eternals), and Armadillo waves round out a packed year. Pinless joints become standard, and Fan Channel exclusives flow through specialist retailers.

milestones.text: 32-inch Galactus at $399.99 draws 14,000 backers — the biggest ML ever.
Pinless joints debut around 2020 and become standard.
Exclusives flow through the Fan Channel at specialist retailers (e.g. Quasar, Summer 2021).

years.headline: Twenty years
years.summary: A premium 20th Anniversary Series 1 celebrates the 2002 Toy Biz debut — Captain America, Iron Man, Hulk, and Toad with retro-style packaging, as Fan Channel exclusives. The Rintrah (Multiverse of Madness), Korg (Love and Thunder), Bonebreaker, Controller, Infinity Ultron (What If...?), Attuma (Wakanda Forever), and Khonshu (Moon Knight) waves fill the year, and Pulse Con 2022 kicks off a new X-Men retro team-uniform line with Wolverine.

milestones.text: A special premium 20th Anniversary line updates the characters from the very first 2002 Toy Biz wave — Captain America, Iron Man, Hulk, Toad — with retro-style packaging, as Fan Channel exclusives (Spring 2022).

sources.label: Bleeding Cool — X-Men retro team uniforms

milestones.text: Pulse Con 2022: a new X-Men retro line in team uniforms kicks off with Wolverine — card-backed, $24.99, April 2023.

waves.baf: Rintrah (Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness)

years.headline: Plastic-free and Epic
years.summary: Packaging goes plastic-free with bioPET windows. The 24-inch Giant-Man HasLab at $199.99 finishes with 13,876 backers — while Ghost Rider's Engine of Vengeance becomes the line's only failed HasLab. Hasbro launches the kid-focused 4-inch Epic Hero Series at $9.99 at Target. The Puff Adder, Cassie Lang (Quantumania), Cosmo (GotG Vol. 3), Ch'od, Amadeus Hulk, Mindless One, Hydra Stomper MK II (What If...?), Across the Spider-Verse Wave 1, X-Men '97 Wave 1, and No Way Home waves fill the year.
years.packaging: Plastic-free: bioPET windows replace open packaging (April 2023).

milestones.text: 24-inch Giant-Man at $199.99 finishes with 13,876 backers. Ghost Rider's Engine of Vengeance becomes the line's only failed HasLab.
Hasbro launches the Marvel Epic Hero Series: kid-focused 4-inch figures at $9.99, found at Target.

waves.baf: Cassie Lang (Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania)
Cosmo the Spacedog (Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3)

spotlight.name: Wolverine
spotlight.why: X-Men '97 Wave 1 — the animated renaissance begins.

years.headline: The animated renaissance
years.summary: The Void, Zabu, and Blackheart (Strange Tales) waves anchor the year, with X-Men '97 Wave 2, Deadpool & Wolverine Wave 1, and Across the Spider-Verse Wave 2 riding the animation wave. Standard MSRP reaches $24.99.

milestones.text: Standard MSRP reaches $24.99; deluxe $30–50; box sets $40–90; HasLab $200–400.

years.headline: First Steps
years.summary: The Nemesis (Uncanny X-Force), Executioner, Gamerverse Legends, Fantastic Four: First Steps, and X-Men '97 Wave 3 waves fill the year, and the Magic: The Gathering crossover figures launch with foil card versions.

milestones.text: Marvel Legends × Magic: The Gathering figures launch at $39.99 each, with a foil version of the card each figure is based on.

years.headline: Retro blisters return
years.summary: 2026 goes retro: blister cards with mini-comic pack-ins, a deliberate throwback to the Toy Biz clamshell era. The archive holds the Box BAF wave, Deadpool & Wolverine Waves 2–3, and Avengers: Doomsday Wave 1 so far. 2026 covers releases observed through 2026-10-11 — see the pre-order tracker for what's next.
years.packaging: Retro blister cards with mini-comic pack-ins.

milestones.text: 2026 = retro blister cards + mini-comic pack-ins; no new packaging overhaul.
Mini Comics Wave 3 pre-orders October 6, 2026 at $27.99 — with a mini comic per figure.
Spider-Man: The Animated Series retro wave pre-orders September 29, 2026 (ships Dec 2026–Jan 2027); X-Men '97 retro wave pre-orders October 21, 2026.
NYCC 2026: Avengers: Doomsday Wave 2 pre-orders October 14, 2026; the made-to-order Bastion & Bolivar Trask 2-pack ($74.99) ships ~November 2027.

NYCC 2026 final-day panel (Oct 11): confirmed rosters + pre-order dates — X-Men '97 wave (Death Gambit, team-suit Cyclops, Jean Grey, Vindicator, X-Factor Havok + Polaris) pre-orders Oct 21; Avengers: Doomsday Wave 2 (Lord Doom Concept Series, Beast, Nightcrawler) pre-orders Oct 14; Astonishing X-Men Cyclops & Wolverine reissue pre-orders Oct 28; YFNS Spider-Man vs. Rhino 2-pack on sale at Pulse Nov 1. The official Maximum Symbiote Spider-Man was shown at the pre-show showcase.

sources.label: Mephitsu — NYCC 2026 Hasbro Marvel Legends panel (Oct 11, 2026)

milestones.text: Pre-order window check (Oct 11, 2026): Oct 14 Doomsday Wave 2, Oct 21 X-Men '97, Oct 28 Astonishing 2-pack all confirmed on schedule; Doomsday wave-1 Cyclops showed Sold Out at Hasbro Pulse; Spider-Man (Marvel Holiday Special) pre-orders opened Sep 23 as reported (general release).

Mid-October research sweep (Oct 12, 2026): Oct 14 Doomsday Wave 2, Oct 21 X-Men '97, Oct 28 Astonishing 2-pack and the Nov 1 YFNS sale all reconfirmed on schedule; Doomsday wave-1 aftermarket documented cooling (Gambit $79.99 → $25.99, Cyclops $64.99 → $40.99) — the Chronicle's first launch curves; Super-Skrull reissue added to the tracker ($46.99–$47.99, Fan Channel, Oct–Nov 2026).

packagingEras.text: Oversized clamshell blisters with a 32-page reprint comic pack-in, inherited from Toy Biz's Spider-Man Classics line.

packagingEras.text: Hasbro's packaging drops the comic pack-in; new molds drop Toy Biz's signature finger joints, but the Build-A-Figure theme continues.

packagingEras.name: Window box
packagingEras.text: The 2014 Infinite Series retool moves the line to box packaging with bigger BAFs and more accessories at a $19.99 MSRP.
